name: Blessed Python pin set as of 2026-07-13
short_definition: Opinionated blessed dependency and runtime pin snapshot for greenfield Python services in the engineer monorepo stack as of 2026-07-13, aggregated from leaf research versions_as_of fields. Default: CPython 3.13, uv 0.11.28, ruff 0.15.21, basedpyright 1.39.9, FastAPI 0.139.0, Pydantic 2.13.4, SQLAlchemy 2.0.51, asyncpg 0.31.0, uvicorn 0.51.0, httpx 0.28.1, pytest 9.1.1, plus auth/obs/worker companions. Labels are research pins — re-resolve with uv lock before ship; review_by 2026-10-13.
scope_in: Runtime and tooling pins (Python, uv, ruff, basedpyright, ty status)
Web stack pins (FastAPI, Starlette, uvicorn, Granian optional, httpx)
Workers (Taskiq line; Celery/Temporal as tier notes)
Explicit non-default / avoid list with replacements
scope_out: Application business dependencies (LLM SDKs vary by product)
Exact patch pins for every transitive (uv.lock is source of truth per app)
Guaranteeing PyPI will still resolve these exact versions after review_by

runtime.free_threading: opt-in only (3.14 officially supported FT; not default for async APIs)
runtime.cpython_3_14: bugfix OK when deps verified; not silent default

quality.ty: 0.0.58 beta editor only — not sole CI gate

workers.temporal: pin SDK in lock when used

use_when: Comparing PR dependency diffs to blessed set
do_not_use_when: Blindly upgrading brownfield without changelog review
Forcing Granian/msgspec/Temporal when tier doesn't need them
alternatives: App uv.lock always wins at runtime
Org private mirror may lag — document divergence

do: Start from this snapshot then uv lock for exact transitive graph
Pin uv version in CI to match policy
Keep requires-python aligned with basedpyright pythonVersion and ruff target-version
Label optional tiers (Granian, msgspec, Temporal, Celery) clearly
dont: Don't commit floating == without lock for apps
Don't install pydantic v1 alongside v2
Don't default python-jose, Black, Poetry, mypy-only
Don't use arq for brand-new systems without explicit reason
Don't treat research pins as eternal — they are as_of labeled

code_skeleton:
# pyproject.toml — blessed greenfield skeleton (as_of 2026-07-13)

[project]
name = "example-service"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = [
  "fastapi==0.139.0",
  "pydantic==2.13.4",
  "pydantic-settings==2.14.2",
  "uvicorn[standard]==0.51.0",
  "httpx==0.28.1",
  "sqlalchemy[asyncio]==2.0.51",
  "asyncpg==0.31.0",
  "pyjwt[crypto]==2.13.0",
  "structlog==26.1.0",
  # add redis/taskiq/supabase only when needed
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  "ruff==0.15.21",
  "basedpyright==1.39.9",
  "pytest==9.1.1",
  "pytest-asyncio==1.4.0",
  "httpx==0.28.1",
  "testcontainers[postgres]==4.14.2",
]

[tool.uv]
exclude-newer = "7 days"

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"

[tool.basedpyright]
pythonVersion = "3.13"
typeCheckingMode = "recommended"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
markers = ["unit", "integration"]

# .python-version
# 3.13

# CI: UV_MALWARE_CHECK=1 uv sync --frozen --all-groups
#     uv run ruff format --check . && uv run ruff check .
#     uv run basedpyright && uv run pytest -m unit && uv audit
failure_modes: Pins drift from lockfile → 'works on my machine' CI
Mixing pydantic v1/v2 → import and FastAPI errors
asyncpg + transaction pooler without mitigations → production incidents
CI uv older than 0.11.16 → malware check unavailable
Optional stacks (Celery/Granian) silently added → ops surprise
anti_patterns: Copying this snapshot into every service without removing unused deps (Taskiq/Supabase/OTel only when needed)
Pinning ty as required prod dependency
Using gunicorn+uvicorn hybrid by cargo cult

deprecation_watch: uv audit still preview-ish since 2026-06 — pin uv CLI
ty pre-1.0 — do not make sole CI gate until stable
python-jose / passlib legacy samples in blogs
setup-uv action major lines — pin commit SHA
ts_boundary: TS app keeps pnpm lock and Next pins (stack-rules). Shared contracts via OpenAPI versions, not shared Python pins. Node  version policy is independent.
rust_boundary: Rust uses Cargo.lock/Axum stack in rust.md. No attempt to unify version numbers across languages. Handoff is architectural not pin-level.
supabase_boundary: supabase-py 2.31.x for product APIs; SQLAlchemy/asyncpg for direct SQL. Supabase platform versions (JS client, CLI) follow TS modules — only Python client pins live here.
boundary_contracts: OpenAPI generated from FastAPI version in this pin set
JWT algorithms compatible with Supabase/IdP issuer
Migration tool versions (Alembic vs supabase CLI) chosen per ownership model
